title: partner-sku-drift-detection-and-listing-remediation-guidance
content:
Purpose:
This note defines a pragmatic detection + remediation flow for SKU and listing drift across cloud marketplaces (AWS, Azure, GCP). Aim is to reduce listing mismatches that cause billing/UX breakage, and to give clear ownerable runbooks for partner-facing and internal remediation. This is a working doc for Partner Ops + Product + Engineering to iterate on.

Context / problem statement:
- We see frequent small-but-high-impact mismatches between published marketplace tiles and internal entitlements: SKU names, trial durations, pricing tiers, region availability, and required entitlements (KMS, private images).
- Drift surfaces as: customer-reported failed trials, incorrect metering, duplicate SKUs, and marketplace rejections during audits.
- Current remediation is ad hoc: partners get an email, engineering triages, PRs land slowly, updates miss one of the three clouds.

Definitions (short):
- SKU drift: any divergence between the currently published marketplace metadata and our canonical product spec (pricing, entitlements, trial length, billing dimensions).
- Canonical spec: single source-of-truth YAML/CSV in repo 'marketplace-assets' (owner: partner-ops/product).
- Listing artifact: tile metadata, icon, short description, long description, entitlements checklist, technical bundle (container/AMI/ARM).

Detection design (what we should measure):
1) Daily asset sync validation job (owner: infra/marketplace-runner):
   - Pull published listing metadata via each cloud vendor API (tile metadata, SKU ids, effective price, trial flags).
   - Compare against canonical spec files.
   - Emit 3 classes of anomalies: metadata mismatch, missing SKU, unexpected additional SKU.
   - Report in a daily digest to Slack channel #mp-drift-alerts and create Jira tickets for severity=high.
2) Telemetry signals (owner: observability):
   - Failed trial activations per SKU (rate and absolute count).
   - Metering-reconciliation delta: billed units (marketplace) vs internal usage logs over rolling 7-day window.
   - Marketplace rejection events (publisher portal rejection codes).
3) Customer-facing triggers (owner: customer-success):
   - CS cases tagged with 'marketplace-fail' auto-create an incident linked to the SKU.

Classification & severity rules (simple):
- P0: Missing SKU in marketplace (customers cannot provision) or price materially lower/higher than canonical (>10% delta).
- P1: Trial mismatch (trial offered but backend not provisioned) or entitlement flag mismatch causing access errors.
- P2: Copy difference (short/long description mismatch) or nonexistent but low-impact metadata mismatch.

Remediation playbook (owner matrix incl. partner-ops, product, eng):
Step 0: Triage (automated)
  - Daily job creates a ticket with diffs attached and assigns to partner-ops on-call for triage.
  - If customer-impacting (P0/P1), page on-call SRE + partner-ops lead.
Step 1: Root cause categorization (owner: partner-ops + product)
  - Is canonical spec out of date? -> update canonical spec, create PR to marketplace-assets repo, tag product review.
  - Is the published listing stale (vendor portal drift)? -> partner-ops initiates cloud portal update (see cloud-specific runbooks below).
  - Is this a downstream build/CI problem (artifact mismatch)? -> link to release-engineering and block the next rollout until fixed.
Step 2: Fix and verify (owner: engineering / partner-ops)
  - For canonical spec changes: PR -> code owners review -> merge -> release script updates marketplace packages.
  - For portal-only fixes: partner-ops applies change in vendor portal and records merchant ticket id.
  - Post-change: trigger validation job to confirm parity and run a smoke provisioning test that provisions a trial and validates entitlement state.
Step 3: Communication
  - Internal: update Jira ticket and post remediation summary in #mp-drift-alerts with links to PRs and portal tickets.
  - Partner-facing (if partner-managed): use templated email (copy below) and update partner status page.
  - Customer-facing (if customers impacted): CS to send targeted outreach templates.

Cloud-specific quick notes (runbooks):
- AWS Marketplace:
  - Common failure modes: changed pricing dimension name, subscription SKU duplication, AMI vs container mismatch.
  - Runbook pointer: check seller central > product listings, compare SKU IDs and 'pricingDimensions' array to canonical CSV.
  - Action: submit an 'update listing' package and attach the merged canonical spec.
- Azure Marketplace:
  - Common failure modes: offer plan mismatch, missing managed identity flag, private plan gating.
  - Runbook pointer: Partner Center -> Offers -> Plans. Export JSON and diff.
  - Action: update plan JSON or request publisher support for backend plan refresh.
- GCP Marketplace:
  - Common failure modes: deployment template mismatch, region gating, wrong Billing SKUs.
  - Runbook pointer: Cloud Marketplace partner portal -> product -> artifacts.
  - Action: re-upload deployment config and associate correct Billing SKU.

Operational checklist (for a single drift ticket):
- [ ] Confirm anomaly via validation job logs and attach diff snapshot.
- [ ] Tag severity and estimate customer impact (users/devs/contracts).
- [ ] Identify owner path: canonical fix vs portal fix vs infra bug.
- [ ] Create PR or portal change and assign reviewers.
- [ ] Run smoke-provision and metering check after change.
- [ ] Close ticket with postmortem note if P0/P1.

Sample partner-facing copy (short email + marketplace tile variants):
- Email subject (partner ops): "Action required: Listing parity issue detected for SKU <SKU-ID>"
- Email body (concise): "Hi <PartnerName>,

We detected a mismatch between the listing you have published and the canonical product spec Redwood maintains. This may cause provisioning or billing issues for customers. We created ticket JIRA-XXXX and propose the following next steps: 1) confirm the attached canonical spec, 2) approve the portal update or share required edits, 3) confirm after you apply the change. If you'd prefer, Redwood can apply the portal update on your behalf.

Thanks,
Partner Ops — Redwood Inference"

Marketplace tile copy variants (examples to maintain parity but tuned per cloud):
- AWS short tile (<=80 chars): "Redwood Inference — Low-latency LLM inference (pay-as-you-go)"
- AWS long tile (<=350 chars): "Run high-throughput LLM inference with predictable latency and per-token pricing. Choose Hosted, Dedicated, or Private deployment modes; includes enterprise features like KMS integration and telemetry. Free 14-day trial; cancel anytime."
- Azure short tile (<=70 chars): "Redwood Inference: Production LLM inference, enterprise-ready"
- Azure long tile: "Ship LLM features with consistent latency and cost controls across regions. Supports dedicated GPU pools, VPC/private deployments, and in-console traceability for token costs. 14 day trial for qualified customers."
- GCP short tile: "ML inference runtime optimized for latency and cost"
- GCP long tile: "Deploy inference with automatic batching, prefix caching, and smart routing. Integrates with cloud IAM and KMS for secure workloads. Contact sales for trial."

Template: PR description checklist when updating canonical spec (marketplace-assets repo):
- Title: "canonical: sku <SKU-ID> — update <field> — reason <short>"
- Description: include link to drift ticket, diff snapshot, and owner approvals.
- Files changed: list canonical YAML/CSV path.
- CI checks required: unit tests for asset validator, smoke provisioning job.

Metrics & success criteria (what counts as improvement):
- Reduce P0 incidents from marketplace drift by 70% within 90 days of rollout.
- Mean time to remediate P0: < 24 hours, P1: <72 hours.
- Automate detection for 95% of common drift classes (metadata mismatch, missing sku, price delta).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Which team will own the canonical spec approval policy for pricing changes? (product or finance?)
- Do we enable auto-remediation for low-risk copy-only mismatches (e.g., update short/long tile copy automatically)?
- What SLAs should we promise partners for portal-applied changes vs Redwood-applied changes?

Appendix: quick snippets for CS to use when customers hit trial provisioning failures:
- CS short reply: "We're aware of an issue with the marketplace trial for <SKU>. We've opened ticket JIRA-XXXX and are prioritizing remediation. We'll follow up by <date/time> with a resolution or mitigation steps."

Notes and next steps (action items):
- Partner Ops: start a 30-day pilot running the daily validation job and owning triage. (owner: Miguel)
- Observability: add metering-reconciliation dashboards and an alert for >5% delta over 7 days. (owner: Priya)
- Engineering: add a smoke-provisioning job to CI that exercises trial provisioning for all new SKU merges. (owner: Samir)
- Product/Finance: decide on pricing change approval flow and documented threshold for when manual approval is required.

This file is a working draft; feedback please add inline comments and flag any cloud portal steps that are inaccurate based on your publisher admin access.
